prompt:
Research the official free-tier limits of the GitHub Actions service for public and private repositories (minutes, storage, concurrency). Cite the GitHub documentation page you used.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the official GitHub documentation, the limits for GitHub Actions differ significantly between public and private repositories, particularly regarding cost and minute quotas. Below is a breakdown of the free-tier limits for minutes, storage, and concurrency.

### Minutes and Billing
For **public repositories**, the use of standard GitHub-hosted runners is free and unlimited. For **private repositories**, users receive a monthly quota of free minutes based on their plan, after which they are billed. Self-hosted runners are always free to use regardless of repository visibility.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "The use of standard GitHub-hosted runners is free: In public repositories" | CLAIM: Standard GitHub-hosted runners are free for public repositories.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "GitHub Actions usage is free for self-hosted runners and for public repositories that use standard GitHub-hosted runners." | CLAIM: Self-hosted runners and public repository standard runners do not incur costs.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "For private repositories, each GitHub account receives a quota of free minutes, artifact storage, and cache storage for use with GitHub-hosted runners, depending on the account's plan." | CLAIM: Private repositories have a specific free quota for minutes and storage based on the user's plan.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "GitHub Free | 500 MB | 2,000 | 10 GB" | CLAIM: The GitHub Free plan includes 2,000 free minutes per month for private repositories.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "Larger runners are always charged for, even when used by public repositories or when you have quota available from your plan." | CLAIM: Larger runners are not free, even for public repositories.

### Storage Limits
Storage limits apply primarily to private repositories or when exceeding free tiers. Artifact storage is shared with GitHub Packages, while cache storage has a separate allowance per repository. GitHub Support cannot increase storage limits.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "GitHub Support cannot increase storage limits for GitHub Actions." | CLAIM: Storage limits are fixed and cannot be increased via support tickets.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "The artifact storage amounts shown are shared with GitHub Packages. This means your total storage across Actions artifacts and GitHub Packages storage cannot exceed the included amount for your plan." | CLAIM: Artifact storage and GitHub Packages share the same storage quota.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "Cache storage: Actions cache storage is a separate allowance of 10 GB per repository." | CLAIM: Cache storage is allocated separately at 10 GB per repository, regardless of the plan.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "GitHub Free | 500 MB | 2,000 | 10 GB" | CLAIM: The GitHub Free plan includes 500 MB of artifact storage.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions | QUOTE: "GitHub Enterprise Cloud | 50 GB | 50,000 | 10 GB" | CLAIM: The GitHub Enterprise Cloud plan includes 50 GB of artifact storage.

### Concurrency and Rate Limits
Concurrency limits restrict how many jobs or workflows can run simultaneously or be queued. These limits apply to check runs, workflow triggers, and concurrency groups.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "A check suite can have a maximum of 50,000 check runs." | CLAIM: There is a limit of 50,000 check runs per check suite.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Each repository is limited to events triggering a workflow run. 1500 events / 10 seconds / repository" | CLAIM: Repositories are limited to 1,500 workflow trigger events every 10 seconds.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "500 workflow runs / 10 seconds" | CLAIM: A maximum of 500 workflow runs can be queued every 10 seconds.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "When using `queue: max` in the `concurrency` section, up to 100 workflow runs / concurrency group" | CLAIM: Concurrency groups can queue up to 100 workflow runs.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Standard GitHub-hosted runner | Free | 20" | CLAIM: The Free plan allows 20 total concurrent jobs on standard GitHub-hosted runners.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Standard GitHub-hosted runner | Pro | 40" | CLAIM: The Pro plan allows 40 total concurrent jobs on standard GitHub-hosted runners.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Standard GitHub-hosted runner | Team | 60" | CLAIM: The Team plan allows 60 total concurrent jobs on standard GitHub-hosted runners.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "Standard GitHub-hosted runner | Enterprise | 500" | CLAIM: The Enterprise plan allows 500 total concurrent jobs on standard GitHub-hosted runners.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits | QUOTE: "The maximum concurrent macOS jobs is shared across standard GitHub-hosted runners and GitHub-hosted larger runners." | CLAIM: macOS job concurrency limits are shared across runner types.
